_meta.purpose: Development verification set for OVERLAP-AWARE SUPPRESSION (ALL-TOKENS semantics). Authored 2026-08-16 at Task 0 of GATE0-overlap-suppression-plan.md, BEFORE the rule existed. ALL data is fictional.
_meta.why_it_exists: The readability failures that motivated this change were observed on burned-set controls. Designing the rule against those exact examples and re-measuring on the same sets is circular. This file is the openly-readable, purpose-built corpus the rule is developed against -- the address_verify_samples.json pattern. The four burned sets stay REGRESSION GATES ONLY and never inform the rule.
_meta.standing: NOT a gate. NOT quotable. NOT blind batch v4 and no substitute for it. It is committed on purpose: visibility is its purpose, exactly as visibility would destroy a holdout.
_meta.composition: 24 samples in four classes. (a) reach: multi-token SAP jargon where EVERY token is already protected -- must produce no redaction. (b) both-directions VALUE class: real PII values that CONTAIN a protected token -- must survive. (c) both-directions PERSON class: glossary words used as people -- the +/-40-char backstop must still win. (d) controls: zero-PII prose including street-type words as ordinary nouns.
_meta.semantics_under_test: ALL-TOKENS (Gate 0 Q2): a span is suppressed only if EVERY whitespace token in it is in ALLOWLIST_EXACT or matches is_custom_sap_object, AND every token clears the user-context backstop at ITS OWN offsets (Q5).
_meta.reading_the_note_field: `note` explains what a sample probes. It is NEVER transmitted to the service. Annotation text inside a `text` field is a named trap class in docs/HANDOVER.md (metadata-as-payload); this file keeps them structurally separate.
_meta.known_limit: Class (a) asserts on scrub() output end to end, never on a span list. Span boundaries are the engines' to choose, so an assertion about which span was emitted would be an assertion about GLiNER's tokenizer rather than about the rule.

samples.text: FSD ZMM_PRICE_SYNC was signed off before the sprint started.
samples.note: Two adjacent tokens, both protected: FSD is in the built-in seed, ZMM_PRICE_SYNC matches the custom-object rule (underscore = unambiguously technical). The canonical reach case.

samples.text: Escalated to Basis DEV for the interface rebuild.
samples.note: Basis (module) and DEV (env) are both glossary entries and adjacent. Exact-token matching cannot see a span covering both.

samples.text: The RFC EDI bridge dropped every message overnight.
samples.note: RFC and EDI, both glossary modules, adjacent.

samples.text: GL FX postings failed again after the period close.
samples.note: GL and FX shipped in 1.2.1. Two-character tokens, below the SAP_USER_ID floor, so these arrive from the spaCy layer.

samples.text: Checked the QMEL LALE mapping and it is still correct.
samples.note: QMEL (table) and LALE (doc), adjacent, no user-context cue anywhere in the window.

samples.text: Both /IWFND/MAINT_SERVICE and ZSD_OUTPUT_CTRL are registered in the target client.
samples.note: Namespace shape and Z-shape, each unambiguously technical, so the backstop is bypassed per token by design.

samples.text: Raised against FSD ZFI_DUNNING_RUN during the MDG cutover.
samples.note: Three protected tokens across two spans-worth of text. MDG shipped in 1.2.1.

samples.text: The transport moved from QAS to PRD without an incident.
samples.note: SINGLE-token protected spans, no cue. Regression guard: the pre-change path must keep behaving identically -- ALL-TOKENS is a generalisation, not a replacement.

samples.text: Remittance advice should go to PO Box 5512, Napier 4110 from next month.
samples.note: R1's test. PO is a glossary entry sitting INSIDE a real postal address. Whole-span containment suppression un-redacts this; ALL-TOKENS must not, because Box/5512/Napier/4110 are not protected.

samples.text: Deliver the replacement pallet to 18 Kestrel Rise, Cambridge 3434.
samples.note: Rise is a glossary process noun AND a street type. The collision the glossary's own rejection list warned about, on the value side.

samples.text: Site contact is at 7 Kowhai Way, Tauranga 3110 and the gate code changed.
samples.note: Way is a glossary process noun and an ambiguous street type requiring a trailing comma-locality, which this sample supplies.

samples.text: Invoices for the account now go to PO Box 220, Whangarei 0140, attention Hemi Waititi.
samples.note: A protected token inside one value while a second, unrelated value sits in the same sentence. Suppressing the address must not disturb the person.

samples.text: The DC Terrace office at 42 Rimu Terrace, Napier 4112 takes the returns.
samples.note: DC is a glossary facility token adjacent to the value rather than inside it. Guards against a rule that widens a suppression to a neighbouring span.

samples.text: Bank details for the payer changed; new IBAN is NZ42 0099 1122 3344 5566 77.
samples.note: A structured value whose whitespace tokens are individually meaningless. Confirms tokenisation of a multi-token span does not accidentally make every token unprotected-but-suppressible.

samples.text: Delivery note query reported by Driver, please assign back to the team.
samples.note: Driver is a glossary role AND a plausible surname. 'reported by' is a user-context cue inside +/-40 chars, so the backstop must refuse suppression. A glossary entry vetoes a PATTERN, never CONTEXT.

samples.text: The exception was approved by Payer and logged the same afternoon.
samples.note: Same class, different cue ('approved by' is not in the frozen cue list -- 'approver' is). Deliberately probes the cue boundary rather than assuming the list covers it.

samples.text: Change requested by Rise and countersigned by Way on the same ticket.
samples.note: Two glossary words as two people in one sentence, both behind 'requested by'. If ALL-TOKENS ever merged them into one span the whole span would be protected -- this is the sample that would catch it.

samples.text: Escalated on behalf of Basis, who raised it during the night shift.
samples.note: 'on behalf of' is in the frozen cue list. Basis is a module name being used as a person, which is the shape that makes suppression dangerous.

samples.text: Movement type 561 posts against the storage bin in the DC overnight.
samples.note: DC as an ordinary facility abbreviation, no cue. Must be suppressed exactly as today.

samples.text: Rise in open items after the MRP run still needs review before month end.
samples.note: Rise as an ordinary noun in sentence-initial position -- the position the per-token PERSON lottery is worst at.

samples.text: Court, Terrace, Close and Drive are all valid street types in the configuration table.
samples.note: The four PRE-CLEARED-BUT-UNSHIPPED street types as ordinary nouns. None is in the glossary, so nothing here may be suppressed -- this sample must NOT become the evidence that ships them.

samples.text: Output determination did not trigger for the collective run this morning.
samples.note: Zero protected tokens anywhere. If a redacting span appears here, the change reached something it should not have.

samples.text: The interface between the two plants is stable and no data was affected.
samples.note: Interface is a glossary module used as an ordinary noun; plants is not protected at all. Mixed span, must stay unsuppressed under ALL-TOKENS.

samples.text: Reversal posted, PGI repeated, and the OSS note was applied without error.
samples.note: Three separate single-token glossary entries in one sentence, none adjacent. Confirms the change does not depend on adjacency.
